_: One or two plain sentences per release, for the people who use Sirius rather than build it, shown at the top of each release on /changelog/. Derived from `git log vA..vB` between the tags and the release notes in PROJECT-STATE.md — say only what the commits did. A release with no entry here shows its commit list alone; add the new tag's line when a release is cut.
v1.118.10: The first start opens Get started with Sirius — seven steps from connecting a model to choosing a theme — instead of a VS Code sign-in screen and a Copilot walkthrough. New: Sirius: Turn On Tab Completion. Install from VSIX and the issue reporter no longer fail on a Sirius patch.
v1.118.9: The editor's download, documentation, license and privacy links now open siriuside.com instead of GitHub.
v1.118.8: Images you paste or attach reach the models that can see them; Ask, Edit and Agent each get their own tools, and the agent's file tools stay inside your workspace. Thinking is shown, Tab completion works on llama.cpp, local servers can take an API key, commit messages use your default model, and Sirius no longer overrides three of the editor's shortcuts.
v1.118.7: Linux arm64 gets .deb and .rpm packages, and its tarball and server now hold the same glibc 2.28 floor as x64. The update server no longer offers the server tarball to arm64 desktops, and the Arch repository's publish step was hardened.
v1.118.6: The remote server tarballs (Linux x64 and arm64) ship with every release, the Arch pacman repository now updates with each tag, and the new Sirius icon replaces the old one on every platform. The arm64 build of this release needs glibc 2.38; v1.118.7 lowers that to 2.28.
v1.118.5: The first .deb and .rpm packages. New: next-edit prediction (off by default), project rules and ambient context, image input carried to each provider that accepts it, tool sets sized to the model, prompted tools for local models without a tool API, and the integrated browser on by default.
v1.118.4: One command imports settings, keybindings, snippets and extensions from VS Code, Cursor, Windsurf or VSCodium. Sirius also refuses to load Ollama models above 12 GB by default, after one froze a machine; the limit is a setting.
v1.118.3: The agent now acts in the project whatever the model's size: a curated tool set for small models, edit and create-file tools whose changes land in the editor's diff-and-checkpoint review, and a recovery net for models that write tool calls as prose.
v1.118.2: Chat works out of the box: Sirius is the editor's default chat agent, so there is no Copilot sign-in prompt, and a default model always exists. Tab completion is rebuilt on the local model's native fill-in-the-middle — debounced, cached and cancellable, and off until you turn it on.
v1.118.1: The first Sirius-authored patch release. Agent edits now go only through the editor's reviewed edit path, and the commit-message and merge-conflict actions in Source Control work.
v1.118.0: The first public release: Linux (x64 and arm64) and Windows (x64), built in CI from the tag, with a build-provenance attestation on every asset and delivery through the update server.
